correctness.rationale: With the pairing linear in the first variable, the adjoint coefficient at the kernel centered at A_jw+b_j is the conjugate weight times exp((||A_jw+b_j||²−||w||²)/2); its modulus is e^(||b_j||²/2) times that of the entire compensated weight. For a generic complex line tv the Gram blocks with the same A_j are fixed up to unitary phases under Weyl translation; distinct translation centers give positive definite blocks by restriction of the exponential relation to a Vandermonde line. Off-block overlaps tend to zero uniformly as |t|→∞ since (A_i−A_j)v≠0. Thus the bounded adjoint gives a lower Gram bound for the coefficient estimate on the complement of a disk on every such line. Liouville and density force the compensated weights to be constant, nonzero by hypothesis. Conversely the Gaussian change of variables gives an isometry, onto by the inverse affine composition and reciprocal weight. In the averaged energy, unequal linear parts give vanishing cross terms by rescaling and dominated convergence off ker(A_i−A_j). For equal A, with a=Aw, the coherent-kernel overlap phase Im⟨a+b_j,a+b_i⟩ together with the adjoint phases gives exactly 2 Im⟨a,b_i−b_j⟩+Im⟨b_j,b_i⟩, a nonconstant real character; its normalized ball average tends to zero. Monomial testing shows weak escape of normalized kernels; hence any compact adjoint contributes vanishing averaged squared norm. The essential-norm estimate follows. The parity choices of chirp make it periodic mod N and every nonzero shift gives a geometric sum of ratio exp(2πih/N); hence the Fourier modulus is sqrt(N) on every homogeneous degree. This attains the bound with b_j=0 for all N,d in scope. The packaged checker and 9448-check diagnostic claim were inspected, not executed; analytic arguments establish the general claims.

value.rationale: The unitary-affine boundary is the natural Gaussian-norm-preserving regime and still permits noncommuting matrices, coincident linear parts and distinct translations. The theorem rules out cancellation even between initially unrestricted entire weights and identifies a usable, symbol-independent coefficient norm modulo compacts. The exact energy and sharpness at each N make that quantitative separation meaningful, beyond recalculating single-operator criteria. It does not settle the broader nonunitary multivariable problem or claim equality for arbitrary coefficients.
